categories.main_business_segments: IAC operates through several primary business segments: Dotdash Meredith (digital and print publishing), Angi (home services marketplace), Care.com (online care services marketplace), Search (Ask Media Group and Desktop search/content sites), and Emerging & Other (including Vivian Health, The Daily Beast, IAC Films, and formerly Mosaic Group and Roofing). Each segment targets distinct markets and operates under multiple brands.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: IAC leverages proprietary digital platforms, content management systems, and data-driven algorithms for content creation, user matching, and advertising. Dotdash Meredith utilizes expert-driven editorial processes and proprietary ad products like D/Cipher for intent-based targeting. Angi and Care.com use matching algorithms and background checks to connect users with professionals and caregivers, while Search relies on search algorithms and partnerships (notably with Google) for paid listings and content delivery.
categories.primary_customers_markets: IAC serves a broad range of customers: consumers seeking information, home services, or care solutions; advertisers and marketers targeting these audiences; professionals and caregivers seeking clients; and enterprise clients (via Care.com’s B2B offerings). Key end markets include U.S. households, advertisers, SMBs in home services, families needing care, and healthcare employers (Vivian Health).
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are primarily U.S.-focused, especially for Dotdash Meredith, Angi, and Care.com, but Angi also operates internationally in Canada and several European countries (UK, Germany, France, Netherlands, Austria, Italy). Emerging & Other includes some international activities, and Search properties have global reach via the internet.
categories.supply_chain_position: IAC operates downstream in the digital media, online marketplace, and services supply chain, directly interfacing with end consumers, advertisers, and service professionals. It acts as a platform and intermediary, facilitating transactions, content delivery, and connections between buyers and sellers or service providers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding digital reach and monetization (especially for Dotdash Meredith), enhancing proprietary ad and matching technologies, adapting to changes in digital advertising (e.g., cookie deprecation), and leveraging AI for content and licensing. R&D is focused on platform improvements, new product features, and data-driven personalization, with ongoing investment in mobile, AI, and user experience.
categories.revenue_model: IAC generates revenue through a mix of digital and print advertising, affiliate and performance marketing, subscription and membership fees (for both consumers and professionals), licensing and syndication, transaction fees, and enterprise contracts. Search revenue is heavily reliant on paid listings supplied by Google, while Dotdash Meredith and Care.com have diversified revenue streams including subscriptions and licensing.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: IAC faces competition from diversified media companies, online publishers, search engines, social media platforms, generative AI services, traditional offline media, and specialized marketplaces (e.g., Thumbtack, HomeAdvisor, Sittercity). Its brands are generally leaders in their categories (e.g., Dotdash Meredith in digital publishing, Angi in home services), but face intense competition for consumer attention, advertiser budgets, and professional participation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, IAC reported $3.8 billion in revenue, down 13% year-over-year, reflecting declines in Angi, Search, and Emerging & Other, partially offset by growth in Dotdash Meredith Digital. Adjusted EBITDA was $380 million (up 13%), with significant cash reserves ($1.8 billion) and $1.9 billion in net long-term debt. The company is in a period of portfolio transition, with recent divestitures and a planned spin-off of Angi.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: IAC emphasizes trusted, expert-driven content (Dotdash Meredith), efficient and vetted matching (Angi, Care.com), and large, engaged audiences for advertisers. Its platforms offer breadth of services, proprietary technology for targeting and matching, and strong brand recognition. Differentiation is built on quality, authority, user experience, and the ability to adapt quickly to digital trends and regulatory changes.
